expected_result: The DMS sign-in form is visible.
voice_text: This is the new D M S web application. It is a multi tenant document management system for small and medium organizations. Every person belongs to one organization, and sees only what their role and each document allow. This walkthrough uses a fictional organization called Demo Industries, with sample documents. You will sign in as an employee, a reviewer, an administrator, a department manager and a project manager.

expected_result: The Documents page lists documents with classification and status chips.
voice_text: Sameer is an employee in the Finance department. He signs in with his work email and password. The password is typed into a masked field. After sign in, the document library opens. It lists only the documents Sameer is allowed to see, with the category, classification, status, version and size of each.
subtitle_text: Employee signs in and sees the document library

action: Search for acme, then filter by classification.
expected_result: Acme documents are listed; the filter keeps confidential documents only.
voice_text: Search looks through titles, file names, metadata and the text inside documents. Searching for acme finds the invoice and the vendor agreement. The classification filter narrows results further, and counts are calculated only over documents Sameer may see, so nothing leaks through the numbers.
visual_instruction: Search for acme, then filter by classification.

expected_result: Details, metadata, versions with Preview and Download buttons, and the retention date are shown.
voice_text: Opening a document shows its details. The invoice carries the metadata its category requires, such as the invoice number and vendor, the date until which it must be kept, and its version history. Preview and download are separate rights. Each issues a short lived secure link, and every download is recorded in the audit log.

action: Open Upload, choose the Contracts category, select a file, fill the required fields and upload.
expected_result: A success message says the document is waiting for approval.
voice_text: Now Sameer uploads a contract. He chooses the Contracts category, picks the file, and the form asks for what that category requires: a department and a contract reference. The category is configured so that documents are reviewed before release, and the form says so. The file is checked for its real type and scanned before it is stored.
subtitle_text: Upload a document that needs approval
visual_instruction: Open Upload, choose the Contracts category, select a file, fill the required fields and upload.

action: Sign out, sign in as the reviewer, open Approvals and approve the new agreement.
expected_result: The review dialog opens and the item leaves the queue after approval.
voice_text: Meera is a reviewer. After she signs in, the menu shows how many approvals are waiting for her. She opens the new service agreement, reads the history, and approves it with a comment. A rejection would require a reason. Nobody can approve their own upload, and every decision is recorded.
visual_instruction: Sign out, sign in as the reviewer, open Approvals and approve the new agreement.

action: Sign in as the administrator and filter by Archived.
expected_result: The administrator sees the salary letters and the archived guidelines.
voice_text: Asha is the organization administrator. Her library includes documents others cannot see, such as the highly confidential salary letters, and archived documents. Administrator access to restricted documents is an audited privilege, so every use leaves a record. Filtering by status shows the archived remote work guidelines.
visual_instruction: Sign in as the administrator and filter by Archived.

expected_result: The Restore from archive button is shown.
voice_text: Documents have a lifecycle. An approved document can be archived, which keeps it readable but closed to new versions and edits, and an archived document can be restored. Categories also define how long a document must be kept and when it should be reviewed. Legal holds and approved deletion already work in the system programming interface, and will get screens in a later release.

action: Open Organization and browse the tabs.
expected_result: Departments, projects and employees are listed.
voice_text: The organization page shows the departments, branches, projects and designations that documents are filed against, and the employee directory. Access rules use this structure. For example, confidential finance documents are visible to the Finance department and to its manager.
visual_instruction: Open Organization and browse the tabs.

voice_text: The account page lists exactly what the signed in person is allowed to do. Roles grant actions, such as upload, approve or archive. Whether a person can open one particular document is decided separately, from its classification, its owner, its department and project, and any direct sharing.

action: Sign in as the department manager.
expected_result: Finance documents are listed, the salary letters are not.
voice_text: Rohan manages the Finance department. He sees the confidential finance documents for his department, including invoices and contracts, because the access policy gives department managers visibility into their own department. He does not see the salary letters, which belong to Human Resources.
visual_instruction: Sign in as the department manager.

action: Sign in as the project manager and open Shared.
expected_result: The shared invoice is listed with view and download access.
voice_text: Priya manages the Apollo project. An employee shared the Acme invoice with her directly, with permission to view and download. The shared page lists what has been shared with you and what you have shared with others. Sharing can expire, can be withdrawn at any time, and never gives more than the person role already allows.
visual_instruction: Sign in as the project manager and open Shared.

voice_text: This first release of the web application covers sign in, the document library with search and filters, document details with versions and retention, upload with validation, approvals, sharing lists, lifecycle archiving, the organization directory, and role based permissions. Still to come are the screens for sharing and uploading new versions, administration of users and categories, reports and dashboards, and notifications. Thank you for watching.
subtitle_text: What is available and what comes next
